events.title: Richard the Lionheart marries Berengaria in Cyprus
events.description: During his conquest of Byzantine-ruled Cyprus on the way to the Third Crusade, Richard I married Berengaria of Navarre at Limassol. The island became a long-lasting crusader kingdom.
events.html: During his conquest of Byzantine-ruled Cyprus on the way to the Third Crusade, Richard I married Berengaria of Navarre at Limassol. The island became a long-lasting crusader kingdom.

events.title: Casimir the Great founds a university in Kraków
events.description: King Casimir III founded the Kraków Academy, now the Jagiellonian University. It is the oldest university in Poland, where Nicolaus Copernicus later studied.
events.html: King Casimir III founded the Kraków Academy, now the Jagiellonian University. It is the oldest university in Poland, where Nicolaus Copernicus later studied.

events.title: Florence Nightingale is born in Florence
events.description: Florence Nightingale, named after her birthplace, was born to a wealthy English family. Her work in the Crimean War and her use of statistics reshaped nursing and hospital care.
events.html: Florence Nightingale, named after her birthplace, was born to a wealthy English family. Her work in the Crimean War and her use of statistics reshaped nursing and hospital care.

events.title: Airship Norge crosses the North Pole
events.description: Roald Amundsen, Umberto Nobile and Lincoln Ellsworth flew over the Pole in the airship Norge on a flight from Svalbard to Alaska. It is the first undisputed arrival at the North Pole.
events.html: Roald Amundsen, Umberto Nobile and Lincoln Ellsworth flew over the Pole in the airship Norge on a flight from Svalbard to Alaska. It is the first undisputed arrival at the North Pole.

events.title: Red Army opens its offensive at Kharkov
events.description: Soviet forces attacked around Kharkov in Ukraine to regain the initiative. German forces encircled the attackers within days, and the disaster cost the Red Army more than 200,000 men.

events.title: Soviet Union lifts the Berlin Blockade
events.description: After almost eleven months, Soviet authorities reopened road and rail routes into West Berlin. The Allied airlift that had supplied the city became a defining episode of the early Cold War.
